title: Snapless zoom rail and column composition profiles for analytic grids
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers building analytic UIs need more fluid control over table density and column composition when switching between exploratory (wide) and compact (dense) modes. Current behaviors rely on hard snap breakpoints and simplistic 'collapse priority' lists which cause jarring layout shifts and frequent manual re-adjustment of column widths.

Goal: Design a new interaction and token set that enables: 1) a continuous "zoom rail" control to smoothly transition density without snapping; 2) column composition profiles (named presets) that capture priority, min/max widths, and collapse strategies for common analytic layouts; and 3) fractional/responsive resize behavior so column widths can align to visual rhythm (not just pixel snaps), improving perceived stability during reflow and while virtualized rows are loading.

Deliverables:
- Interaction spec for a snapless zoom rail (mouse + trackpad + keyboard + touch) with accessible keyboard controls and ARIA announcements.
- Visual tokens and density scale (0.6x..1.4x) and mapping to typography, row height, cell padding, and icon scale.
- Column composition profile schema (preset names, editable user profiles, fallback logic) and UX for applying/pinning profiles per view.
- Fractional-resize guideline: support sub-pixel widths with rendering fallback for browsers that round, and a heuristic to avoid layout thrash during continuous resize.
- Transition rules for virtualized table viewport (prefetch margins, sticky summaries, and placeholder skeleton sizing consistent with density).
- High-fidelity mocks and an interactive prototype in Figma demonstrating zoom rail, profile picker, and resize gestures.

Design constraints and tradeoffs:
- Avoid building a heavy new controller in the table component that duplicates routing/URL state; profile application should be a lightweight state hook with optional persistence by the host app.
- Performance budget: interactions must maintain 60fps on middle-tier laptops; avoid expensive layout reads during drag by using transform-based previews until drop.
- Accessibility: keyboard-only users must have a way to switch density presets and step the zoom rail in 5% increments; screen readers must hear concise announcements when profile/preset changes occur.

Success metrics:
- Reduced manual column adjustments: target 30% fewer user-resizes in telemetry for analytics customers after rollout.
- Fewer layout-related support tickets in 90 days post-release.
- Positive UX score in follow-up usability study (>80% task success for switching density and restoring layout presets).
comments: 2025-03-11 - PM review (Jared O'Neil): Like the profiles idea; please map two enterprise personas (analyst, ops) to default presets and include migration strategy for saved layouts.

2025-03-12 - Engineering sync (Lead: Priya Menon): Raised runtime concerns about continuous resize triggering relayouts in older browsers. Proposed prototype with transform preview + commit on mouseup. Eng to provide microbenchmarks by 3/18.
2025-03-13 - Accessibility review (Ravi Singh): Confirm keyboard steps and ARIA live-region copy. Recommend announcing "Density: Compact (0.85x) applied" rather than raw numbers.
2025-03-14 - Design critique (team): Adjust visual tokens to preserve baseline rhythm at 0.7x; reduce icon scale delta at smallest density to maintain hit targets. Agreed to iterate in prototype.
2025-03-14 - QA note (Elena Torres): Add test cases for RTL and zoom-level persistence when switching routes.
